dimensions.name: Relationship recovery under a prescribed specification
Relationship discovery from data alone
dimensions.justification: Structured screening and adoption validated on planted-truth tasks with characterized false-discovery control (anchor 4). Common permutation rule: TPR 1.000 (linear 30/30, nonlinear 40/40, interaction 10/10), FDR 0.167 (2.8% outside the S2 residual-tree draws; half the 0.310-0.459 FDR of the tree ensembles), silent on 5/5 null tasks. Reported formula (mboostrs native claim): TPR 0.912 (nonlinear 40/40, linear 25/30, interaction 8/10), FDR 0.039 (down from 0.645), silent on 5/5 null tasks, and 5/5 scale-only detections on S3. Real-data published effect directions: 104/113 (92.0%). Held below 5 because residual-tree splits on S2 raise permutation FDR and active-term pruning drops weak linear terms when a dominant interaction absorbs >95% of risk reduction.

dimensions.name: Experimental iteration speed
dimensions.justification: Scorecard session, 50,000 x 20, ten follow-up fits with prediction and permutation importance: median 3.04 s, p90 7.19 s, total 39.75 s (anchor 3: seconds per fit; 2.2x faster than CatBoost's 6.69 s median and 11.3x faster than the 2026-11-21 baseline of 34.4 s). Median fit-plus-predict on the 95-table real battery is 17.1 s under the 64-fit standard budget (vs. 50.5 s for EBM). Not sub-second (anchor 4).

dimensions.name: Robustness across conditions
dimensions.justification: Completes 269 of 285 real-data runs (94.4%, up from 70.9% and ahead of EBM's 91.2%). Small-n real tasks: 12/12 completed with median loss 9.8% below the reference (ahead of CatBoost -8.0%, XGBoost -0.8%, LightGBM +7.0%); lowest loss of all six libraries on S5 (n=200, MSE 0.268). Half point below 3 because 16 runs still fail rather than degrading gracefully: 8 in conformal_interval on LSS models with adopted interactions (NotImplementedError), 5 from out-of-domain test values entering log/sqrt transforms, and 3 edge cases (mixed str/None sort, interaction margin missingness, degenerate sqrt knot).

dimensions.name: Uncertainty honesty (calibration)
dimensions.justification: Split-conformal 90% intervals across 156 regression runs: median coverage 0.901, 93.6% within 0.85-0.95, 1.9% below 0.85, with sharper median width/SD 1.523 (down from 1.722). On the heteroscedastic task S3, coverage by tercile of the scale variable is 0.894/0.906/0.908, demonstrating adaptivity (anchor 4). Binary median ECE 0.0355. No demonstrated warning when an interval is unreliable under shift (anchor 5).

dimensions.name: Reproducibility and auditability
dimensions.justification: Predictions identical on rerun for 10/10 datasets (exact SHA-256 match to 1e-12). fit returns a structured DecisionTrail with provenance (version, git sha, seed, threads), candidate evaluation history, and active final formula. One-command reproduction of an entire discovery report is not demonstrated (anchor 4).

dimensions.name: Predictive validity
dimensions.justification: Beats the prespecified reference on 33/38 regression (Wilcoxon p = 7.2e-6, median ratio 0.847) and 31/46 binary tasks (p = 0.034). Median gap to the best complete library drops to 9.0% on regression (within 5% on 17/38) and 7.5% on binary (within 5% on 20/46), ahead of LightGBM (9.9% / 30.7%) and XGBoost (19.3% / 35.7%) on both tracks; paired against CatBoost on regression, median ratio is 1.036 (16/38 better, p = 0.16). Lowest loss of all six libraries on 6 of 7 planted tasks (S1, S3-S7) and 0.842 on pure-interaction S2 (down from 9.324, ahead of LightGBM 0.918 and XGBoost 1.712). Half point below 4 because CatBoost still leads in regression within-5% count (33/45 vs 17/38) and 5.6% of real runs do not complete.
